reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain is a well-known and thoroughly debunked neurological myth. Scientific consensus from neurologists and cognitive scientists, supported by advanced neuroimaging techniques such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) scans, demonstrates that virtually all parts of the brain are active throughout the day. Even simple tasks or periods of sleep engage nearly the entire brain over time. Furthermore, brain tissue that goes unused typically atrophies or degrades, yet healthy adults do not possess large regions of dormant brain mass.
